South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 12/25/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent shortness of breath, productive cough with greenish sputum, and worsening fatigue.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax is seen for follow-up two days post-admission for exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) complicated by pneumonia. He reports minimal improvement in his condition, with ongoing significant dyspnea at rest and with minimal exertion. The productive cough continues to yield thick green sputum, and he notes that the frequency of nebulizer treatments remains at every hour.
The patient also reports persistent fevers, now averaging 100.5F, and an increase in overall malaise, which he feels is exacerbated by his respiratory condition. He expresses concern regarding his lack of improvement and the potential for further complications, including respiratory failure.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + increased fatigue, + intermittent fevers, - weight loss, - chills, + night sweats. Pulmonary - + persistent productive cough with greenish sputum, + increased wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 128/74 mmHg - Heart Rate: 90 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 30 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 87% on supplemental oxygen (4 L via nasal cannula).
General: The patient appears fatigued and is in moderate respiratory distress, utilizing accessory muscles for breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Severe wheezing on auscultation; decreased breath sounds bilaterally; prolonged expiration with prominent rhonchi; crackles audible throughout lung fields.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation with persistent bacterial pneumonia, evidenced by continued respiratory symptoms and hypoxemia despite ongoing treatment. 2. Persistent hypoxemia requiring increased supplemental oxygen; consideration for escalation of respiratory support if no improvement is observed. 3. Increased risk for respiratory failure; close monitoring and potential intervention are warranted.
PLAN
1. Continue intravenous Levofloxacin 750 mg daily; adjust based on culture sensitivities and clinical response; consider adding coverage for atypical pathogens if no improvement in 48 hours. 2. Repeat chest CT scan to evaluate for possible pulmonary complications, including abscess formation or worsening pneumonia. 3. Maintain supplemental oxygen at 4 L via nasal cannula; if saturation continues to decline, consider non-invasive ventilation (NIV) for respiratory support. 4. Increase oral Prednisone to 80 mg daily to enhance anti-inflammatory effects; reassess in 48 hours. 5. Consult Infectious Disease for further evaluation and potential modification of antibiotic therapy based on clinical status and imaging results. 6. Continue physical therapy consultation for respiratory rehabilitation and to improve functional status as tolerated. 7. Monitor vital signs and respiratory status closely; prepare for potential transfer to the ICU if clinical deterioration occurs.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax remains hospitalized, with ongoing focus on optimizing respiratory support and managing his COPD exacerbation and pneumonia. The treatment team will continue to closely monitor his clinical status, emphasizing timely interventions to prevent complications. He is encouraged to communicate any changes in symptoms or concerns regarding his treatment plan.
